task: Operator refills the part tray while the robot runs
hazardous_situation: Arm or gripper strikes the operator's hand, arm or torso in free space (transient contact)
rationale: Without limiting, a 14 kg payload at full speed can break bones (S2). Tray refill happens several times per hour (F2). The motion is visible and the trained operator can step back (P1). Judgment call, see open point OP-1.
design_measures: Rounded links, no sharp edges, padded gripper
information_measures: Operator training; floor marking of the collaborative workspace

task: Operator refills the part tray while the robot runs
hazardous_situation: Hand is trapped between gripper or workpiece and the tray or fixture (quasi-static contact)
rationale: Crushing can cause irreversible injury (S2). Hands are in the tray area several times per hour (F2). Approach to the tray is slow and predictable (P1).
design_measures: Fixture and tray designed with gaps that avoid trapping fingers (ISO 13854) where possible
information_measures: Operator training; pictogram at the tray

hazardous_situation: Hand or forearm is pinched between two robot links as a joint closes
rationale: Irreversible injury possible (S2). Operator is regularly within reach (F2). Joint motion is visible and slow near the operator (P1).
design_measures: Link geometry leaves clearance at joints; programmed paths avoid folded poses

task: Operator leans over the table to reach a part
hazardous_situation: Arm or gripper contacts the operator's head or face
rationale: Head and face are the most sensitive body regions (S2). Leaning in is occasional (F1). The operator looks at the part and not at the arm (P2).
design_measures: Base height and layout keep programmed paths below shoulder height

task: Operator refills the part tray while the robot runs
hazardous_situation: Moving workpiece edge slides across the operator's hand or forearm
rationale: Cuts normally heal (S1). Hands are in the area several times per hour (F2). A thin edge is hard to see and avoid (P2).
design_measures: Gripper holds parts with machined edges facing away from the operator; parts are deburred upstream

hazardous_situation: Gripper loses the workpiece on loss of power or air and it falls on the operator's foot
rationale: Reversible injury with safety shoes (S1). Operator is often present (F2). A falling part cannot be avoided (P2).
design_measures: Gripper is self-locking and keeps its grip on loss of power

task: Operator clears a jammed part with the robot paused
hazardous_situation: Robot starts to move while the operator's hands are in the gripper or fixture
rationale: Irreversible injury possible (S2). Jam clearing is occasional (F1). A start from standstill comes without warning (P2).
information_measures: Procedure for jam clearing; indicator lamp shows paused state

task: Programmer teaches positions standing next to the arm
hazardous_situation: Arm moves faster or further than expected while the programmer is within reach
rationale: Irreversible injury possible (S2). Teaching is occasional (F1). The programmer is very close and focused on the tool (P2).
information_measures: Only trained programmers may use manual mode

hazard: Hazardous motion continues in an emergency
hazardous_situation: A person sees a dangerous situation and has no way to stop the robot
rationale: Covers situations the other functions did not foresee (S2). Emergencies are rare (F1). The endangered person may be unable to act (P2).
information_measures: E-stop locations shown in the operating instructions

hazardous_situation: Arm drops under its own weight on loss of power or brake failure and traps a hand
rationale: Irreversible injury possible (S2). Hands are under the arm only occasionally (F1). The arm sags slowly and can be avoided (P1).
design_measures: Spring-applied brakes on all joints (power-off = braked)
information_measures: Instruction for releasing a trapped person without power

task: Electrician works on the open controller cabinet
hazardous_situation: Contact with live parts in the controller
rationale: Electric shock can be fatal (S2). Maintenance is occasional (F1). Live parts cannot be seen (P2). Handled by electrical design and procedure, not by a control safety function.
design_measures: Electrical equipment per IEC 60204-1; lockable main disconnect; touch-safe terminals

task: Technician changes the gripper or payload settings
hazardous_situation: Payload, tool or limit values are wrong so force and speed limiting no longer work as assessed
rationale: The limits are what keep contact harmless, so a wrong value removes the protection (S2). Changes are occasional (F1). The error is invisible to the operator (P2).
information_measures: Validation checklist to be completed after every parameter change
